diagnostic_class.definition: >=3 rings and an exocyclic ring alkene
diagnostic_class.status: DIAGNOSTIC POSITIVE CONTROL ONLY. Known from hand inspection of thiothixene. It is NOT a production filter and no selector optimises for it; the question is only whether a blind sampler represents a class that is 7% of its own admissible pool.

findings: Library-mean ranking is SYSTEMATICALLY broken, not unlucky: it is deterministic, so its zero is a fact rather than a p=0.06 draw. Library mean is the mean oracle of molecules CONTAINING a payload -- a prevalence statistic -- and it is anti-correlated with the rare structural classes that carry the gain.

An EQUAL family quota is 2.3x WORSE than uniform (1.03 vs 2.33, p(zero) 0.36 vs 0.095) because it under-samples whichever family holds most of the pool: region_replace is 4,978 of 5,937 here and contains the entire class.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM: I read a single 32-arm draw of zero as proof the stratifier suppressed the class. At a 7.14% base rate p(zero) under uniform is ~0.095, so one zero proves nothing. The 200-seed census is what settled it.

Plain random loses a family that is small BY CONSTRUCTION: region_excise is 30 of 5,937 (0.5%) and was absent from 84 of 100 draws. Hence a small reserved floor per family plus unbiased sampling for the remainder.
